title: Almohad Caliphate
capsule: The Almohad Caliphate arose from Ibn Tumart's Berber reform movement among the Masmuda of the High Atlas and became an empire when his successor Abd al-Mu'min overthrew the Almoravids and captured Marrakesh in 1147, ruling Morocco, the western Maghreb and Muslim Iberia as caliphs claiming sole religious authority in the Islamic West. Under Ya'qub al-Mansur the Almohads crushed Castile at Alarcos in 1195, but defeat at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212 triggered a long collapse; the last Almohad, Idris al-Wathiq, was murdered at Marrakesh in 1269 as the Marinids seized the city.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases (Times Atlas of World History; Kinder & Hilgemann; Shepherd 1926) at ~0.07° resolution. Coastal Maghreb and Andalusi cores are well attested; Saharan limits are conventional lines through thinly governed territory — shown with low confidence. (Almoravid-era shapes share this entry before c. 1150.) Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: high).
